subject: Two problems from Mom's 7/15 relayed feedback: (1) the three stacked text boxes inside #unified-input (Mama's Perspective per-card note, the general 'Set it down' field, the Garden Guru composer) — an IA diagnosis + resolution; (2) the plant-ownership surface Paul wants to give her (picture she selects + clear description + zone), currently framed as an editable table of 26 plants, 24 of which need a zone and ~24 a real photo.
review_level: flow / IA (both problems cross screens and write-targets)

user_context.primary_user: Mom. Validated: daily user (~4.5 sessions/day), mobile-only iPhone, reads with difficulty and often without glasses (the only device to use the A/A+ toggle — 12 events), one-handed and reclined, half-engaged. Zero usage of every affordance that required her to originate, explore, or navigate (star: 0/104 revisits; seeded prompts: 0). Answered 2 of 2 Mama's Perspective recognition-cards on 7/13 — the one affordance that has ever worked.
user_context.secondary_user: Paul — authors questions, folds answers to canon, reads her feedback out-of-band.
core_jobs_to_be_done: Mom: tell Paul something about the place that's on my mind, and be sure it actually reached him.
Mom: make the record of MY place actually about my place — my picture, where it really lives — without it becoming a chore I resent.
Mom: answer a specific question about the ground only I'm standing on, in one tap.
Paul: collect ground-truth (zone links, real photos, corrections) that only someone on the property can give, and see it land in canon.
user_context.context_of_use: iPhone PWA, in bed with coffee or winding down, half-attended, often no glasses; sometimes on the property standing in front of the plant. Weak rural signal. She does not read fine print, and does not reliably distinguish UI elements by their labels.
assumptions_made: Her three asks are one ask — ownership of the record — per the 7/16 relay's synthesis. This is Paul's read of her, not her words; her verbatim was lost.
The relay is INCOMPLETE (stated in the source doc). There may be more she said that Paul didn't recall.

'She wants a clearly labeled general feedback field' is a relayed paraphrase. I treat the INTENT (a distinct, findable, dependable place to tell Paul things) as real; I do NOT treat the literal solution ('a label') as her design instruction — she reads with difficulty, so a label cannot be the mechanism that carries it.
That she'd engage with per-plant ownership at all is unproven. n=2 recognition-taps is the entire evidence base for her contributing anything.
user_context.user_context_confidence: medium — her behavior is well-validated; her 7/15 words are lost and reconstructed one remove from source (provenance: paul-relayed).

principles_applied: The glance and the repository and the loop — invite the one input only someone at the property can give, and fold it back visibly (Tate-Tracker/CLAUDE.md governing principle)
Meaning must land via icon + size + color + position, not label text (memory: project_fernwood_mom_reading_accessibility) — LOAD-BEARING for both problems
Make every surface read at half-engagement (fernwood.md)
Scope is communicated by where you tap, not auto-detected (cross-project) — the diagnostic lens for the three boxes
Register is carried by chrome, not just words — especially for the no-glasses reader (fernwood.md candidate) — three write-targets wearing one skin is the same failure inverted
Save-success at the surface, not at the destination (cross-project) — and its honesty corollary: never claim a save you haven't verified
Field journal, not task manager (CLAUDE.md) — governs the whole plant-table question
Convert origination asks into recognition asks (proposed 2026-07-13, now with n=2 supporting evidence)
For a user whose only validated behavior is 'opens and glances,' an affordance must live where she already looks (fernwood candidate, 2026-07-13)
Nielsen #1 visibility of system status; #4 consistency; #6 recognition over recall; #2 match between system and the real world
Norman — signifiers must differentiate; identical form implies identical function

problem_1_diagnosis.what_the_code_shows: All three boxes live inside ONE section — `<section class="unified-input" id="unified-input">` (viewer.html:4803). In DOM order: `#mom-queue` (4807) which renders the Mama's Perspective card containing a '＋ Add a note' button revealing a `.mom-queue-correction` textarea (8720-8736, 8789-8796), then `buildGeneral`/`expandGeneral` (8642-8679) appending a SECOND `.mom-queue-correction` textarea to the same host, then `.ui-input-row` with `#ui-textarea` (4812). Three text-entry surfaces, one container, ~300px of vertical space.
problem_1_diagnosis.the_actual_IA_problem:
It is NOT 'three boxes.' It is THREE DIFFERENT WRITE-TARGETS WEARING THE SAME FORM, distinguished only by the one channel this user cannot use — label text.

Write-target A — per-card note (`.mom-queue-correction` inside the card) → POST /api/feedback with context.type='mom-queue', scoped to questionId. Meaning: 'this is about THAT question.'
Write-target B — general note (`.mom-queue-correction`, second instance) → POST /api/feedback, kind 'open', questionId of a placeholder. Meaning: 'this is about anything.'
Write-target C — composer (`#ui-textarea`) → ObservationStore (verbatim, AI-free) THEN Garden Guru. Meaning: 'log this and answer me.'

A and B are rendered by the SAME CSS CLASS. Same 1px #cdbf90 border, same #fffdf6 fill, same Crimson 15px, same rows=2, same 44px min-height (viewer.html:3703-3708). They are pixel-identical. C differs only by being borderless inside a warm-tan row. So the entire semantic difference between 'this is about the crocosmia question' / 'this is about anything' / 'ask the Almanac' is carried by three lines of italic 13.5px #5a5238 helper prose — precisely the fine print her documented constraint says she cannot route by.

She is not confused because there are three boxes. She is confused because the app rendered three different promises in one costume and asked her to read the difference.
problem_1_diagnosis.the_tension_resolved: She asked (relayed) for a general field 'clearly labeled as such' — i.e. MORE distinct, not fewer boxes. That is not in conflict with consolidation; it is a diagnosis she supplied in the only vocabulary available to her. 'Labeled' is her word for 'I could tell which one this was.' Labeling is the mechanism she named; distinctness is the property she wants. For a reader with her constraint, a label CANNOT deliver distinctness — so honor the ask by delivering the property through position, chrome, and persistence, and do not congratulate ourselves for shipping a bolder label. Concretely: give her ONE always-present, visually-other, positionally-fixed place to tell Paul things — and remove the two impostors that look like it.

problem_2_diagnosis.the_reframe: Her ask is an END-STATE about the plants ('every plant should carry a picture I chose, a clear description, a zone'). Paul has translated it into a TOOL ('a table she can see and edit'). That translation is the error, and it's a specific, nameable one: an end-state about the record was converted into a CRUD surface over the record. She did not ask for an editor. She asked for the record to be true.
problem_2_diagnosis.why_the_table_is_wrong_for_her:
Four independent reasons, any one of which is disqualifying:
(1) A table IS fine print. It's the densest possible text grid — 26 rows × 4 columns of small type, distinguished entirely by label text and column position. It is the single worst form factor for a reader with her constraint. The A/A+ toggle cannot save a table; scaling type just makes it scroll.
(2) It's a task manager. 24 empty cells with a header row is a to-do list with a completion percentage implied by the whitespace. 'Field journal, not task manager' is the project's founding tone rule; a 26-row grid of blanks violates it on sight, before a word is read.
(3) It's origination at scale. Every affordance requiring her to originate has scored zero (star: 0 uses in 104 revisits; seeded prompts: 0). The one thing that ever worked was recognition — a pre-formed question, one tap (n=2). A table is 48 origination acts in a row.
(4) It's a desk surface on a phone. She is mobile-only, one-handed, reclined. A 4-column editable grid is a laptop object.
problem_2_diagnosis.is_paul_reaching_for_a_spreadsheet: Yes — and the tell is in the ask itself. 'Common name, scientific name, location, picture' is the SCHEMA, not the experience. Paul is looking at plants.json (26 objects, 24 with zoneId:null) and picturing the shape of the data, then proposing a UI isomorphic to that shape. That's a builder's mental model rendered as an interface — the classic move of shipping the database to the user. The data has 26 rows; her life does not. She meets one plant at a time, standing in front of it, when it's doing something.
problem_2_diagnosis.the_instrument_problem_this_creates: Paul's stated plan is to ship the table 'and then let her usage prove whether she engages.' This is the most important thing in this review: THE TABLE IS AN INVALID INSTRUMENT. If she doesn't use it, that result is uninterpretable — it cannot distinguish 'she doesn't want ownership' from 'she can't read a table.' Given her constraint, the second explanation is a priori more likely, so a null result would teach nothing while looking like a verdict. Worse, it would produce the exact wrong lesson: 'we gave her ownership and she didn't want it' — retiring a live, unprompted, direct ask on the strength of a rigged test. The star is the precedent: it sat unused for weeks and we still don't know if it was invisible, conceptually wrong, or redundant, because the test couldn't separate them. Do not repeat that with the one thing she has actually asked for.

findings.observation: `sendGeneral()` (viewer.html:8682-8693) calls `postFeedback()` — which fires a `WorkerAPI.call(...).catch(e => console.warn(...))`, a fire-and-forget with a swallowed rejection — and then unconditionally calls `showAck("Noted — it's in the record. ✓")`. The acknowledgment does not await, inspect, or depend on the POST. It renders identically whether the write succeeded, failed, 401'd, or never left the device. This is the mechanism by which her 7/15 words were lost while she was told they were safe. It is the second such incident (first: 2026-07-03).
findings.user_impact: For the make-or-break user, on the make-or-break emotion. Trust is load-bearing at Fernwood (CLAUDE.md), and this surface tells her a confident lie at the exact moment she gives the app something she cares about. She has now spoken into it twice and been swallowed twice. Every other recommendation in this review is worthless if this stands — a better note field that silently discards her words is a worse product, not a better one, because it will harvest more of her trust before spending it. Note the compounding failure: because capture is silent, we cannot even tell WHICH of the three confusing boxes she used on 7/15. The IA problem and the capture problem are hiding each other.
findings.principle_invoked: Nielsen #1 (visibility of system status) + cross-project 'Save-success at the surface, not at the destination' and its honesty corollary — 'don't claim the destination reflects the save until it does'; the same rule the add-species copy already honors ('refresh in 1–3 minutes')
findings.recommendation: Fix this FIRST, before any IA work. Three parts: (a) `postFeedback` returns the promise; `sendGeneral`/`answer` await it and only then show the ack. (b) On failure, do not show a success ack — show an honest, calm, in-place state in the journal register ('Held on your phone — it'll go up next time you have signal.') and queue it. (c) Add a durable local outbox: her verbatim words persist to localStorage BEFORE the POST is attempted (the GENERAL_LOG_KEY write at 8686-8689 already does this for general notes — extend it to card answers, and make it the retry source, flushed on next successful load). The invariant to hold: her words are never only in flight. Belt-and-braces given this has now failed twice on an unknown device-level cause: mirror the outbox to a second key and only clear on a confirmed 2xx.

findings.observation: The per-card note textarea and the general note textarea are the same CSS class (`.mom-queue-correction`, viewer.html:3703) rendered twice, ~120px apart, inside one section. Identical border, fill, font, size, rows, min-height. Their only differentiator is italic 13.5px helper text ('In your words (optional)' vs 'Anything else about the place — a plant we're missing, a date that seems off, something about the app? Set it down here.'). They write to different scopes (questionId-tagged vs open).
findings.user_impact: This is the literal thing she reported. Identical form is a promise of identical function (Norman: signifiers differentiate, or they don't signify). Two objects that look the same and do different things force her to read to route — the exact routing-by-body-text failure her accessibility model rules out. At half-engagement, she doesn't resolve them; she picks one, or she picks neither. On 7/15 we cannot tell which she did.
findings.principle_invoked: project_fernwood_mom_reading_accessibility (meaning via icon + size + color + position, not label text); fernwood 'Register is carried by chrome, not just words'; Nielsen #4 consistency and standards
findings.recommendation:
Reduce the visible text fields in `#unified-input` from three to TWO, and make the two structurally unmistakable.

(1) DELETE the standing '＋ Add a note' button on every card (viewer.html:8789-8794). It is a fourth control competing with three chips and it opens a box identical to the general field. The scoped note keeps its ONE legitimate life: the `correctionPrompt` path on 'Not quite' (8762-8771), where it appears in-place, inside the card, after a tap that has already declared the scope ('Scope is communicated by where you tap'). That is the only moment a question-scoped note is meaningful. NOTE — this reverses Paul's 2026-07-14 steer ('don't want to limit her too much'). That steer was a reasonable inference; she has now reported the resulting surface as confusing. Her direct report outranks the inference (feedback_agent_proposals_not_validated). The capability she loses is 'add a note while tapping Looks right' — which the general field covers, better, because it's always there.

(2) PROMOTE the general field from a toggle-link to a persistent, always-visible field, and give it a durable identity that is not a label. Concretely: move it BELOW the composer, to the bottom of the section, behind a full-width hairline rule (a real separator — 'here begins a different thing'); give it its own chrome that is visually OTHER from both siblings (the composer is a borderless field in a warm-tan row; the card note is a bordered cream box — so this one takes a distinct treatment, e.g. an inset panel in a cooler in-palette green-tint with a left border-rule, echoing the journal's own voice rather than the composer's); size it as a hero field (not rows=2 at 15px — this is the one she asked for; give it presence per 'Discreet ≠ dormant'); and pair it with ONE in-palette identity mark that is taught once and stays constant (per the icon-system rule: it needs a legend entry and a connotation check — a small pencil/journal mark, NOT an ops glyph, NOT an envelope which imports messaging register). Its commit button carries the only words she needs: the destination, in plain language ('Send to Paul' — because that is what actually happens, per 'A CTA's label must promise what the destination delivers'). The identity mark + position + chrome do the routing; the words are confirmation, not the mechanism.

Standing-box doctrine note: this deliberately violates 'never a standing box / defer affordances pending signal.' That gate exists to prevent shipping affordances on Paul-wants with no user signal. She asked for this one, unprompted, in her own words. The gate is satisfied — this IS the signal it was waiting for.

findings.observation: With the boxes resolved, the section's vertical order still needs to encode meaning by position. Current order: Mama's Perspective card → composer → (general foot-line). The three surfaces answer three different questions and should read, top to bottom, as an obvious progression.
findings.user_impact: Position is one of the four channels she can actually route by. If the order is arbitrary, we've spent the channel and bought nothing. A stable, meaningful order lets her learn the section once, by shape, and never read it again.
findings.principle_invoked: Freshness sets altitude (cross-project); the glance and the repository; meaning via position
findings.recommendation:
Lock the order and never let it drift:
1. ANSWER PAUL — the Mama's Perspective card. Freshest, most specific, one tap, zero origination. Earns the top. (Already there; `order` is pinned per the 2026-07-14 composer-ordering fix.)
2. ASK THE PLACE — the Guru composer. Her question, her photo.
3. ——— hairline rule ———
4. TELL PAUL — the persistent note field. Origination, hers alone, always there.
The rule between 2 and 3 is load-bearing: it's the visual claim that below it is a different kind of act (talking to a person, not the app). One rule, in-palette, full width. Do not substitute extra whitespace — she needs a mark, not an absence.

findings.observation: On problem 2: the proposed surface is a 26-row × 4-column editable table of plants, from which 24 zones and ~24 photos must be entered. Framed as: ship it, and let her usage prove engagement.
findings.user_impact: See problem_2_diagnosis. Four independent disqualifiers (fine print / task-manager register / origination-at-scale / desk-surface-on-a-phone), and — most damaging — it is an invalid instrument for the very question it's meant to answer. A null result would be uninterpretable but would read as a verdict, retiring her one direct unprompted ask on a rigged test. This is the star mistake with higher stakes, because this time she asked for the thing.
findings.principle_invoked: Field journal, not task manager (CLAUDE.md); project_fernwood_mom_reading_accessibility; 'For a user whose only validated behavior is opens-and-glances, an affordance must live where she already looks'; Convert origination asks into recognition asks
findings.recommendation:
DON'T BUILD THE TABLE FOR HER. Build it for PAUL — he is the one who thinks in tables, who needs to see 24 nulls at once, and who reads fine on a laptop. A Paul-facing gap table (a tool script or a private page listing every plant's missing zone/photo, ranked) is genuinely useful and costs almost nothing: it's the authoring surface that feeds the queue. That's where the table belongs — behind the glass, not in front of her.

Her side gets the surface described in F5. The instrument question gets answered honestly there instead: a valid test of 'does she want ownership' is one where a null result means something.

findings.observation: The form the plant-ownership surface should actually take. Two facts make this easy and both are already built: (a) Mama's Perspective is the ONE affordance she has ever used (2 for 2), and it is a recognition-tap on a pre-formed question at the top of the app; (b) Phase F already runs photo → Worker → GitHub commit → canon, and she has already used it (2 of the 26 plants carry 'Phase F submission' photos — from her own Guru workflow). The ownership loop does not need new machinery. It needs the existing machinery pointed at the gaps.
findings.user_impact: This converts 48 acts of data entry into a sequence of single-tap noticings, each arriving when she's most likely to care, and each visibly changing her record. It's the governing principle exactly: the glance invites the one input only someone on the property can give, and folds it back visibly. Drudgery is not solved by making entry faster; it's solved by never presenting a queue of 24.
findings.principle_invoked: The glance and the repository and the loop (CLAUDE.md governing principle); Convert origination asks into recognition asks; recognition over recall (Nielsen #6); Prefer the platform's native control (cross-project)
findings.recommendation:
TWO SURFACES, both existing patterns, no table.

(A) THE GAP RIDES THE PLANT'S OWN CARD (the repository layer — passive, honest, always true).
Every plant card already exists and she already opens the Plants card (60 views). Where a gap exists, the card says so in the journal's own voice, in the provenance-chip pattern already shipped for varieties (`renderVarietyRow`): a stock photo carries a quiet chip reading 'a picture of the species, not of ours' and a zoneId:null carries 'not placed yet.' This is the honest-uncertainty flag that the governing principle names as the hook — the place we admit an estimate is exactly where we invite the truth. Both chips are tappable; both are optional; neither nags. When she fills one, the chip flips ('your photo · July' / 'Eastern Garden') exactly as the variety chip flips to 'confirmed on the ground.' This costs nothing when she ignores it and is always there when she doesn't. CRITICAL: this is honesty, not a task list — no counts, no '24 remaining', no progress bar, no checkmarks. The chip states what the record IS, not what she owes.

(B) ONE GAP AT A TIME RIDES MAMA'S PERSPECTIVE (the glance layer — active, seasonal, one tap).
Extend `harvest-questions.py` with two new deterministic card types, harvested from the gaps the data already knows about:
  • PLACE-CONFIRM — 'Where does the panicle hydrangea live?' Answer = the 8 zone names as tappable chips (Fairway, Fairway Fringe, Western Garden, Eastern Garden, Pond Area, Lower 40, Stable Grounds, Parking Bank). This is recognition of names SHE knows for places she walks, not reading comprehension — the same cognitive act as 'Looks right.' One tap → zoneId. Show the map thumbnail (zones.json already carries the polygons over `gep-2015-03-leafoff.webp`) with the zone lighting up as she taps a chip, so the confirmation lands visually, not textually. Do NOT use a dropdown (a closed list she must open, read, and scroll is three failures). Include a 'somewhere else / not sure' chip — a correct 'no' still owes a next move, and a wrong zone is worse than a null.
  • PHOTO-INVITE — 'The picture we have of the mountain laurel is a stranger's. Want to put yours in?' One tap → the NATIVE iOS camera/library sheet via a plain `<input type="file" accept="image/*">` (the composer already does exactly this at `#ui-image-file`, viewer.html:4824). She takes the photo the way she takes every photo; iOS does the work; nothing custom to build or break. → the Phase F commit path she has already used twice.

SEQUENCING IS THE ANTI-DRUDGERY MECHANISM — this is the whole answer to 'how does it not become a chore':
  • ONE card at a time. Never 24, never a count, never 'N remaining.' The queue's existing soft-cap and one-at-a-time discipline already do this.
  • RIDE THE SEASON, NOT THE BACKLOG. Rank the gap-harvest by what the plant is DOING right now — `bloom.dates` in-window, `peakDates` active. Ask about the crocosmia when it's blazing orange; ask about the panicle hydrangea when it's in flower. She is then not doing data entry; she is being asked about the thing she just walked past and noticed. That is the field journal doing its job, and it's why this can't be a table: a table has no sense of July. (Direct evidence this works: her 2 answers were both in-season plants she could see.)
  • NEVER TWO ASKS ON ONE CARD. Zone and photo are separate cards. One tap is the contract.
  • SELF-SILENCE, unchanged from the shipped design. If she doesn't bite, it goes quiet.
  • PROMOTE ON SIGNAL, NOT ON HOPE. If — and only if — she answers 2+ gap-cards in one sitting, offer 'one more?' AFTER the second. Do not ship a batch mode on day one; that's the table wearing a disguise. Her behavior earns it or it never exists.

WHAT THIS BUYS PAUL AS AN INSTRUMENT: a valid test. Each gap-card is instrumented (offered/viewed/answered/latency — the rig already exists). If she answers place-confirms but ignores photo-invites, that's a real finding. If she answers none over a full season of in-window asks, THAT is interpretable as disengagement — because the ask was one tap, in her line of sight, about a plant she was looking at, in a form she has already proven she uses. A null result there means something. A null result on a table means nothing.

findings.observation: Her third ask — 'a clear description' — is the one with no gap in the data (26/26 plants have `guide`, `currentSeasonNote`, `soilNotes`) and it is being quietly passed over because the schema looks full. The relay's own synthesis names the real problem: the descriptions are about the SPECIES, sourced from reference material. They would describe anyone's garden.
findings.user_impact: If we ship her photo and her zone but the prose still reads like a field guide entry someone else wrote, we've made the record look like hers while it still isn't. That's the deeper version of the same complaint, and it will resurface — probably as her losing interest rather than as feedback, since we've now twice failed to capture her feedback.
findings.principle_invoked: The loop (fold the ground-truth back visibly); the depth filter (feedback_tate_tracker_depth_filter — cover what's actually observed here, never regional completeness); 'user notes supersede book/generic' (the Phase-3 rule already shipped in the add-species drafter)
findings.recommendation: Don't design this yet — but don't let it drop, and don't let 'the field is populated' close it. Two notes for whoever picks it up: (a) the precedent already exists — creeping fig was reframed from book-hardiness to 'it wintered over here' on Mom's single field observation, and the plants.json entry now leads with her read. That's what a description of HER plant looks like, and it came from one sentence she said. (b) The mechanism is therefore not an editor — it's the same recognition loop: an in-season observation card ('the laurel's opening — is that early for it here?') whose verbatim answer supersedes the book prose, per the shipped user-notes-supersede rule. Route this to user-researcher first: her 'clear description' is a relayed paraphrase, and we do not know whether she means 'about MY plant' (the synthesis's read), 'shorter', or 'in words I can read.' Those three want different designs and we should not guess. Flagging as an open question, not a finding to build.

findings.observation: The 7/15 loss was total across all four streams, which the relay reads as device-level (token cleared / PWA cache / offline) rather than a broken field. Nothing on Mom's surface would tell her — or Paul — that her device had silently stopped being able to write. `WorkerAPI.isConfigured()` gates `postFeedback` (8697) with no else-branch: if the token is gone, the POST is never attempted and the ack still fires.
findings.user_impact: A device that cannot save is indistinguishable, from her side, from one that can. She will keep talking into it. This is the failure mode that produced two lost-capture incidents and it will produce a third.
findings.principle_invoked: Nielsen #1 (visibility of system status); 'A value's provenance and freshness must be shown as honestly as the value itself' — applied to the write path, not just the read path
findings.recommendation: Engineering owns the fix; the UX constraints are: (a) `isConfigured() === false` must NEVER produce a success ack — it's the loudest possible failure and currently the quietest. (b) The honest state belongs at the surface, in the journal register, calm — she is not to be alarmed, and 'Held on your phone' is true, accurate, and reassuring where 'Noted ✓' is false. (c) Paul needs the detection, not Mom: `mom-queue-watch.py` already runs 9am/7pm and pings him when she answers — it should also ping on a device that has gone silent while sessions continue (metrics arriving + zero writes = the exact 7/15 signature, and it was detectable). Route the root cause to engineering-partner; this is the third incident's prevention, and it is not a UI problem.

what_id_do_to_viewer_html.note: Concrete and scoped. Ordered by dependency — F1 gates everything.

principles_to_propose.principle: Identical form is a promise of identical function — differentiate by the channel the user can actually route by. When two controls write to different targets, they must not share a visual class. Helper text is not differentiation; for any user who can't or won't read fine print (and at half-engagement that's every user), routing must be carried by position, chrome, size, and a taught identity mark. The tell: two controls whose only difference is their label.
principles_to_propose.rationale: From F2 — `.mom-queue-correction` rendered twice, 120px apart, writing to different scopes, distinguished only by 13.5px italic prose. This is the inverse of the shipped Fernwood candidate 'Register is carried by chrome, not just words' (that one: different content forced into one skin; this one: different FUNCTIONS forced into one skin) — which is itself evidence the underlying rule is broader than either. Norman's signifier principle applied to the label-vs-form gap. Would generalize anywhere (Bolo's forms, the dashboard's controls). Propose as candidate — but note it arguably has 2 occurrences already if you count the 2026-07-07 register review as the same rule seen from the other side. Your call whether that counts.

principles_to_propose.principle: Design the end-state she described, not the tool your schema implies. When a user describes what a record should BE ('every plant should have a picture I chose'), the builder's reflex is to hand them a CRUD surface over the record — which is the database shipped to the user wearing a UI. Ask instead: where does each gap live, and what's the one moment that gap is easiest and most rewarding to close? The tell: the proposed columns are the schema's fields.
principles_to_propose.rationale: From F4 + problem_2_diagnosis — 'common name, scientific name, location, picture' is plants.json recited back as a table. Paul named the risk himself ('is Paul reaching for a spreadsheet because HE thinks in tables?'), which is what makes this worth naming: he can see it in the moment and still reach for it, so it wants a name he can apply on his own. Likely recurs anywhere he's the builder and someone else is the user (Bolo's band-facing surfaces, Houseplants). Candidate — 1 occurrence.

principles_to_propose.principle: A test the user's constraints disqualify her from passing is not a test. Before shipping something to 'let usage prove whether she engages,' ask what a null result would mean. If 'she didn't use it' is fully explained by a known constraint (she can't read it, can't find it, isn't there), the instrument can't produce the finding — but it WILL produce a verdict, and the verdict will be wrong in the direction that retires the feature. Fix the instrument or don't run the test.
principles_to_propose.rationale: From the instrument_problem — the strongest thing in this review and the one most likely to save a real mistake. It's the retrospective lesson of the star (zero usage, three live explanations, no way to separate them, quietly killed) applied prospectively. Fernwood's whole prove-before-build discipline (defer affordances pending signal, hard kill metrics) depends on the instruments being valid, and nothing in the doctrine currently checks that. Arguably 2 occurrences already — star (2026-05-27) and this. Propose to Paul as a full principle if he agrees the star counts.
